content.text: Indications: used mainly for anti-inflammatory effects as first line agents for relief of sxs in chronic inflammatory disease states

: GI (irritation, gastritis, PUD, bleeding), increased bleeding time, decreased GFR, ischemia, acute renal failure, salt/water retention, CHF risk, rash, SJS, asthmatics (bronchospasm, dyspnea, wheezing), aseptic meningitis, exacerbation of anemia, rebound HA
COX-1: constitutive (housekeeping, all tissues) → synth cytoprotective PG (GI)
COX-2: inducible enzyme → rapid ↑when inflam prod
CNS: HA, tinnitus, dizzy      -   renal/hepatic tox: AKF if vol deplete
renal: PGE2/PGI2 maintain renal blood flow → ↓PG → ↑Na/H2O →
edema -> ↓antiHTN meds & ↑AKI (esp CKD, HF, cirrhosis, vol deplete) -unopposed vasoconstrict
GI bleed/ulcer, dyspepsia → take w food
↑serious CV thrombotic events (MI, stroke) -poss fatal (↑if CVD or RF)
-poss fatal (↑risk: age, corticosteroids, anticoag, ulcer hx, ↑dose)
Pt ed: take w food: ↓GI effects
cardiac: ↑CV thrombotic risk -> avoid chronic if CVD hx
preg: avoid ±20wk -> fetal renal dysfun, oligohydramnios
: irreversible inhibition of both COX1 & COX2

: GI irritation, erosive gastritis, increased bleeding time, gastric ulceration/bleeding, salicylism (tinnitus, deafness, HA, confusion, increased pulse & respiratory rates), hyperventilation, respiratory alkalosis, hypersensitivity (rash, SJS/TEN), Reyes syndrome (fulminating hepatitis w/ cerebral edema)
inhibit COX-1 → antiplatelet (platelet life  ~7-10d -⍉synth new TXA2)
Reye's syndrome: avoid in pt <19yr w viral infxn

: cortisol, as well as other steroid hormones, binds to intracellular receptors – the steroid-receptor complex enters the nucleus and acts as a transcription factor to turn on certain genes, causing synthesis of specific proteins which are responsible for its physiological actions
Increases BG, increases protein catabolism from muscle/bone, antagonist of insulin
Inhibits number/activity of cells involved in inflammatory response
Inhibits histamine release from mast cells
Mineralocorticoid effects: salt/water retention, potassium loss
: increased appetite/weight gain, fluid retention, emotional instability, insomnia, indigestion, bitter taste, increased BP/BG

: osteoporosis, GI (ulceration, bleeding), psychiatric (mood, psychosis), cataracts, glaucoma, CV (HTN, edema, hypokalemia), diabetes, hyperlipidemia, Cushingoid syndrome, growth failure, impaired wound healing, adrenal suppression, immunosuppression
MOA: anti-inflam via multi actions on several types of leukocytes
↑bone catabolism or antagonize vit D driven Ca absorb
Stim gastric acid & pepsin prod -> take w food
Admin: IV for critically ill, PO, rectal
: block both beta-1 & beta-2 receptors (heart, airway, vasculature)
: depression, fatigue, N/V, insomnia, SOB, dizziness, lightheadedness, HA, diarrhea, rash
: block beta-1 receptors in the heart
: dizziness, HA, fatigue, weakness, dry mouth/eyes, N/V

: block response to adrenergic stimulation (NE, E) at the beta receptor; indirectly blocks Ca-channels in SA/AV nodes resulting in increased refractoriness, decreased automaticity, & decreased conduction velocity
BP w/in 2 to 3 hr after dosing & @ end of each dosing interval during dose titration (***first dose syncope)
MOA: ↓ O2 demand (exertion & rest) via B1receptor -> ↓ HR, ↓ Contractility, ↓ CO, ↓ BP
pure antagonist OR partial agonist->compete w catecholamine & BB
Dizzy, Confused, Depression, lethargy, insomnia, fatigue
Efficacy: BP, HR, angina, HF, arrhythmia
1st dose @ home -> slow HR/fatigue, non-selective -> ↓ alertness/coord
½ life 4-6hr, Susceptible to hydrolysis via serum esterases
MC —---Class II agents: beta blockers, esmolol, metoprolol, propranolol—-----
MOA: block B1, slow SA node & conduction (AV prolong repolarization) @ SA & AV node
Monitoring: slight ↓ QT, ↑ PRm ↓ SA-AV rates
½ life 6hr, QD dose->blood levels ⍉ as sustained as metoprolol
•drugs that ↓ absorption of levothyroxine: aluminum, calcium, cholestyramine, iron, magnesium, multivitamins, sevelamer, sucralfate
•drugs that ↓ effectiveness of levothyroxine by ↓ conversion of T4 to T3: beta blockers, amiodarone, systemic steroids, PTU
Clin Use:     -    Stable     -    Predictable potency    -    Long 1/2 life
Dosing: wide range available -sensative to dose chg
Diff prod = poss diff therapeutic index
-     ↑thyroid Sx/S: palpitation, sweat, ↓weight, diarrhea, insomnia, anxiety
non-toxic diffuse goiter or nodular thyroid dz (w suppressed TSH)
Monitoring: when dose chg or brand chg -body is sensitive to chg in this med
TSH: 6-8wks after dose chg, Q3M for 1st yr -> annually when stable
Pt ed: if pt experiences hyperthyroid Sx/S -tell us
Caution: start low -recent MI, CAD, arrhythmias
Thyroid — slide extras (not in med-list fields)
lithium -> hypothyroid; amiodarone -> hypo- or hyperthyroid
TSH = most sensitive indicator of hypothyroid function
